message.content:
**Proteins commonly found in the mammalian plasma membrane** | Category | Typical Function | Representative Examples | |----------|------------------|------------------------| | **Integral (Trans‑Membrane)** | Span the lipid bilayer; form pores/transport pathways or serve as signal transducers. | • Na⁺/K⁺‑ATPase
• Voltage‑gated K⁺ channel Kv1.2
• Glucose transporter GLUT1 (SLC2A1)
• Aquaporin‑4 (water pore)
• G‑protein coupled receptors (e.g., β₂‑adrenergic receptor, rhodopsin)
• Insulin receptor (RTK) | | **Peripheral / Cytoplasmic side** | Attach loosely to the cytosolic face; often link to the cortical cytoskeleton or signaling complexes. | • Ankyrin‑G (links Nav channels to microtubules)
• Spectrin α & β chains
• Actinin‑α
• Src family kinases (c‑Src, Fyn) – tethered through SH2 domains | | **Extracellular / Extracytoplasmic side** | Extend into the extracellular matrix or lumen; mediate adhesion, immune recognition, or enzymatic activity. | • Cadherins (E‑cadherin, N‑cadherin)
• Integrins (β₁ integrin subunit)
• Mucins (MUC1, MUC16)
• Cluster of differentiation (CD) antigens (CD45, CD28, CD80)
• Matrix metalloproteinases (MT1-MMP) | | **Lipid‑raft / Caveolae components** | Enriched in cholesterol/sphingolipids; involved in endocytosis, signaling, mechanotransduction. | • Caveolin‑1 (CAV1)
• Flotillin‑1 (FLOT1)
• Cholesterol‑binding proteins (SR-BI) | --- ### How many? *Human cells contain roughly 10–20 k different integral membrane proteins.* Large-scale mass‑spectrometry studies have catalogued over 5 000 distinct plasma‑membrane proteins across various tissues, though only a subset (~200–300) are expressed ubiquitously. --- #### Quick reference list (selected) ``` Na/K ATPase alpha/beta subunits Voltage-gated sodium channel Nav1.7 Aquaporin-1 Glut1 (GLUT1) Rhodopsin Insulin receptor beta chain Beta-2 adrenergic GPCR Cadherin-11 Integrin alphaVbeta3 Cluster of Differentiation 44 (CD44) Ankyrin-G Spectrin alpha II Flotillin-1 Caveolin-1 Matrix Metallopeptidase 14 (MT1-MMP) ``` These represent just a few of the hundreds of proteins that make up the functional “proteome” of the plasma membrane.
message.reasoning:
The user asks: "What are the names of proteins found in the plasma membrane?" They likely expect an answer listing some common types or examples of proteins located in the plasma membrane.

We can provide general categories and examples:

- Integral (transmembrane) proteins: e.g., ion channels (Na+/K+ ATPase), receptors (GPCRs like rhodopsin, insulin receptor), transporters (glucose transporter GLUT1).
- Peripheral proteins attached to inner leaflet: e.g., ankyrin, spectrin, actin-binding proteins.
- Glycoproteins: e.g., CD molecules, mucins.
- Lipid rafts associated proteins: caveolin, flotillin.

Also mention methods used to identify them via proteomics; but question just wants names.
